description: PE Ticket to Completion — drive a single PE-XXXX Jira ticket from triage to a merge-ready MR. Extends the golden Bug-Fix-MR formula and adds what makes it trustworthy unattended: three adversarial CRITIC gates (the fix actually fixes it and is narrow; the test has RED-before/GREEN-after proof; the MR description scores >=8 on root-cause/fix/evidence/screenshots/scope/ticket) plus a per-ticket GARDENER that drives the loop to completion and signs off that all three critics are green and CI is green before a human reviewer is tagged. Invoke from Slack: `/formula pour <id> --var TICKET=PE-XXXX`.

steps.title: {{TICKET}}: Stand up the per-ticket gardener (gb gardener start — type=trigger)
steps.description:
## Gardener setup — drive {{TICKET}} to a merge-ready, critic-green MR

Stand up a per-ticket **gardener** scoped to THIS molecule's subtree. The gardener wakes on a
cadence, triages the molecule's open children, dispatches/nudges work, and drives the loop
until {{TICKET}} reaches a merge-ready MR with all three critics green. Satisfies the
every-gardener-self-blocks rule (advice `ka-0000000974`).

Runs EARLY (right after `check-existing-work`) so the gardener exists before the fix chain
gets going.

> **Firing model (do NOT hand-roll a `type=schedule` bead).** Phase 3b/D10 removed
> `type=schedule` firing entirely — **only `type=trigger` beads fire** (see
> `gardenio/docs/gardener-loop-runbook.md` and `gb gardener start --help`). Use the canonical
> `gb gardener start` endpoint below; it mints the one shape the trigger-engine actually
> fires (`type=trigger` / `trigger:schedule` / `action=spawn_agent`), pins the epic via a
> `gardener-epic:<id>` label, adds a cron pre-flight that only fires while the epic has open
> children, and emits a **bounded default blob** (`run_budget` + a `hard_stop` wall_clock +
> a `bead_query` loop_end + `no_progress_for`) — so it already satisfies advice
> `ka-0000000974` (self-block) without you assembling `stop`/`progress`/`triggers` by hand.

### 1. Discover this molecule's root
This step bead's parent IS the molecule root. Capture it:
```bash
THIS=<this step bead id>   # shown in your assignment
MOLECULE_ROOT=$(kd show "$THIS" --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next((x['id'] for x in d.get('depends_on',d.get('dependencies',[])) if x.get('type')=='parent-child'), ''))")
echo "molecule root = $MOLECULE_ROOT"   # fallback: kd mol list / kd show $THIS
```

### 2. Create the gardener (the one command)
```bash
gb gardener start "$MOLECULE_ROOT" \
  --i-read-the-gardener-instructions \
  --project gardenio \
  --title "gardener-pe-{{TICKET}}: drive {{TICKET}} to a critic-green merge-ready MR" \
  --max-runs 24 \
  --loop-wall-clock 168h \
  --run-wall-clock 30m \
  --terminal-goal "Molecule rooted at $MOLECULE_ROOT is closed: MR !{{MR_IID}} merge-ready with all 3 critics >=8 and CI green." \
  --json
```
`gb gardener start` is **idempotent** — if a gardener is already attached to this molecule it
adopts that one instead of duplicating a loop, and exits non-zero with a link. The default
cadence is a deterministic staggered 30-minute cron seeded from the epic id; pass `--cron`
only if you need a different beat. Capture the printed schedule/trigger bead id — the
`gardener-signoff` step references it.

> The gardener is created **enabled**. If you want it to stay dormant until the fix chain is
> underway, pause it immediately after creation:
> `kd update <gardener-bead-id> -f enabled=false` (re-enable with `-f enabled=true`, or let
> an operator flip it on). Its cron pre-flight already no-ops while the molecule has no open
> children, and its `bead_query` loop_end self-disables once the subtree drains.

### 3. Verify the self-block with the engine's own verdict (never hand-parse fields)
```bash
gb gardener status <gardener-bead-id> --json | jq '.has_backstop, .self_block, .self_block_reason'
# want:  true  "ok"  null   → backstop + wedge-detector both green (advice ka-0000000974)
```
If `has_backstop` is not `true` or `self_block` is not `ok`, the gardener is unsafe — fix it
(raise `--max-runs` / add cadence) and re-verify before proceeding.

## Gate
- [ ] Molecule root discovered and recorded as a comment on this step
- [ ] Gardener created via `gb gardener start` (a **`type=trigger`** bead — NOT `type=schedule`)
- [ ] `gb gardener status … --json` reports `has_backstop=true` and `self_block="ok"` (self-block per advice ka-0000000974)
- [ ] Gardener bead id recorded as a comment on this step (the `gardener-signoff` step references it)

steps.title: {{TICKET}}: CRITIC — does the diff actually fix it, and is the scope narrow?
steps.description:
## How to run a critic gate

You are an **adversarial reviewer**, not the author. Your default posture is skepticism: assume the work is *not* good enough until the evidence forces you to score it >=8. Produce a written verdict, score it 0-10 against the rubric below, and act on the threshold:

1. **Measure** — gather the objective signals the rubric names (the diff, the test output, the MR body). Do not score from memory; read the actual artifact.
2. **Judge** — assign a 0-10 score with a one-paragraph written verdict that cites specific evidence (file:line, a quoted assertion, a screenshot URL). Bands: 0-3 broken, 4-5 weak, 6-7 borderline, 8-9 good, 10 excellent.
3. **Bounce or pass** — record the verdict as a comment on THIS step bead, then:
   - **score >= 8** → PASS. Comment `CRITIC PASS <n>/10` + verdict, close this step, let the chain proceed.
   - **score < 8** → DO NOT PROCEED. Comment `CRITIC BOUNCE <n>/10` + the written verdict naming exactly what must change, then reopen/return to the named bounce target step. The downstream steps stay blocked until the bounce target is redone and this critic re-scores >=8.

## Critic 1 of 3: Fix critic

Adversarially review the committed diff for **{{TICKET}}** on branch `{{BRANCH}}`. Two independent questions, both must hold:

### A. Does it actually fix the ticket?
- Re-read the JIRA ticket's *reported behaviour* (`issue/{{TICKET}}/details.md`).
- Trace the diff: does the changed code sit on the exact path that produces the bug? Could the bug still reproduce after this change (wrong layer, masked symptom, happy-path-only)?
- Is the root cause addressed, or just a symptom papered over?

### B. Is the scope NARROW?
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` — every changed file must be justified by the ticket. Flag drive-by refactors, reformatting churn, unrelated files, dependency bumps, or 'while I was in here' edits.
- A correct fix buried in unrelated changes still scores low — narrow scope is a first-class requirement, not a nicety.

### Rubric (0-10)
| Band | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0-3 | Does not fix the ticket, OR fixes it but touches many unrelated files. |
| 4-5 | Plausibly fixes it but root cause is unproven, or scope has avoidable creep. |
| 6-7 | Fixes the reported behaviour; one or two unjustified hunks remain. |
| 8-9 | Clearly fixes the root cause; every changed line is ticket-justified. |
| 10  | Minimal, surgical, obviously-correct fix; zero collateral. |

### Bounce target
**If score < 8: bounce to `investigate-fix`.** Write a verdict naming the gap ("still reproduces because X" / "files A,B,C are unrelated — revert them") and do NOT let `e2e-test` start. The author re-does `investigate-fix`; you re-score.

steps.title: {{TICKET}}: CRITIC — RED-before / GREEN-after proof the test captures the defect
steps.description:
## How to run a critic gate

You are an **adversarial reviewer**, not the author. Your default posture is skepticism: assume the work is *not* good enough until the evidence forces you to score it >=8. Produce a written verdict, score it 0-10 against the rubric below, and act on the threshold:

1. **Measure** — gather the objective signals the rubric names (the diff, the test output, the MR body). Do not score from memory; read the actual artifact.
2. **Judge** — assign a 0-10 score with a one-paragraph written verdict that cites specific evidence (file:line, a quoted assertion, a screenshot URL). Bands: 0-3 broken, 4-5 weak, 6-7 borderline, 8-9 good, 10 excellent.
3. **Bounce or pass** — record the verdict as a comment on THIS step bead, then:
   - **score >= 8** → PASS. Comment `CRITIC PASS <n>/10` + verdict, close this step, let the chain proceed.
   - **score < 8** → DO NOT PROCEED. Comment `CRITIC BOUNCE <n>/10` + the written verdict naming exactly what must change, then reopen/return to the named bounce target step. The downstream steps stay blocked until the bounce target is redone and this critic re-scores >=8.

## Critic 2 of 3: Test-evidence critic

Adversarially verify that the test written in `e2e-test` genuinely captures the **{{TICKET}}** defect — i.e. it is a real regression guard, not a test that would pass with or without the fix.

### What you must see (the bisection proof)
- **RED before:** captured output (terminal screenshot or `/tmp/*-failure.txt`) showing the SAME test FAILING on pre-fix code, with an assertion error that names the buggy value/state.
- **GREEN after:** captured output showing the SAME test (same file + same test name) PASSING on post-fix code.
- **Assertion specificity:** at least one assertion targets the specific behaviour the ticket reported — not a generic `assert no error` / `assert 200`.

### Adversarial checks
- Could this test pass on UNFIXED code? If the assertion is too loose, it proves nothing — score <= 4.
- Are the failure and success outputs from the *same* test name? A different test in each => not a bisection proof => score <= 3.
- If the step legitimately SKIPPED tests (pure-CSS bug, no e2e coverage), the skip justification must be documented; a skip with no justification scores <= 4.

### Rubric (0-10)
| Band | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0-3 | No RED/GREEN evidence, or failure & success are different tests. |
| 4-5 | Evidence exists but assertion is loose / could pass unfixed / skip unjustified. |
| 6-7 | Real bisection proof; assertion specificity is thin. |
| 8-9 | Clear RED->GREEN on the same test; assertion pins the exact defect. |
| 10  | Above, plus the test is well-placed and would catch a future regression. |

### Bounce target
**If score < 8: bounce to `e2e-test`.** Write a verdict naming what is missing ("no pre-fix failure capture" / "assertion only checks status 200") and do NOT let `draft-mr` start. The author re-does `e2e-test`; you re-score.

steps.title: {{TICKET}}: CRITIC — MR description rubric (root cause, fix, evidence, screenshots, scope, ticket)
steps.description:
## How to run a critic gate

You are an **adversarial reviewer**, not the author. Your default posture is skepticism: assume the work is *not* good enough until the evidence forces you to score it >=8. Produce a written verdict, score it 0-10 against the rubric below, and act on the threshold:

1. **Measure** — gather the objective signals the rubric names (the diff, the test output, the MR body). Do not score from memory; read the actual artifact.
2. **Judge** — assign a 0-10 score with a one-paragraph written verdict that cites specific evidence (file:line, a quoted assertion, a screenshot URL). Bands: 0-3 broken, 4-5 weak, 6-7 borderline, 8-9 good, 10 excellent.
3. **Bounce or pass** — record the verdict as a comment on THIS step bead, then:
   - **score >= 8** → PASS. Comment `CRITIC PASS <n>/10` + verdict, close this step, let the chain proceed.
   - **score < 8** → DO NOT PROCEED. Comment `CRITIC BOUNCE <n>/10` + the written verdict naming exactly what must change, then reopen/return to the named bounce target step. The downstream steps stay blocked until the bounce target is redone and this critic re-scores >=8.

## Critic 3 of 3: MR-description critic

Adversarially review the finalized MR description for **{{TICKET}}** (MR !{{MR_IID}}). A reviewer who never saw the ticket should be able to understand the bug, the fix, and the proof from the description alone.

### Six required elements — each is 0, 1, or 2 points (max 12, normalise to /10)
1. **Root cause** — names the actual cause with a code reference (file:line), not just the symptom.
2. **Fix summary** — 2+ sentences explaining what changed and why it resolves the root cause.
3. **Test evidence** — the RED-before / GREEN-after outputs (or collapsible logs) from the test-evidence step are present and render.
4. **Before/after screenshots** — both render inline (use the upload `url` field, not `full_path`) and are apples-to-apples.
5. **Narrow-scope statement** — an explicit sentence asserting the change is scoped to the ticket, with the changed-file list.
6. **Linked ticket** — the JIRA {{TICKET}} link is present and the ticket was commented with the MR link.

Score = round(sum/12 * 10). Any element scoring 0 caps the overall at <= 6 regardless of the others (a missing required element is a fail, not an average).

### Bounce target
**If score < 8: bounce to `mark-mr-ready`.** Write a verdict listing each element and its 0/1/2 score plus what to add, and do NOT let `gardener-signoff` proceed. The author re-does `mark-mr-ready`; you re-score.

steps.title: {{TICKET}}: GARDENER SIGN-OFF — all 3 critics >=8 and CI green before tagging a reviewer
steps.description:
## Gardener sign-off gate

The per-ticket gardener (created in `gardener-setup`) confirms the ticket is truly merge-ready before a human reviewer is pulled in. This is a **manual gate**: it stays blocked until the gardener works the checklist and clears it. `tag-reviewer` depends on this step, so no reviewer is tagged until sign-off.

### The gardener MUST verify ALL of the following
- [ ] **fix-critic** closed with a recorded `CRITIC PASS` verdict scored **>= 8**.
- [ ] **test-evidence-critic** closed with a recorded `CRITIC PASS` verdict scored **>= 8**.
- [ ] **mr-description-critic** closed with a recorded `CRITIC PASS` verdict scored **>= 8**.
- [ ] **CI is green** on MR !{{MR_IID}} — verify, do not assume:
  ```bash
  glab mr view {{MR_IID}} --json head_pipeline
  ```
  Ignore only the known-flaky jobs the golden formula lists; any real failure blocks sign-off.
- [ ] The MR is marked **ready** (not draft).

### Actions
- **All boxes checked** → record a `GARDENER SIGN-OFF` comment on this bead citing the three critic scores + the green pipeline id, close this step (clearing the manual gate), and let `tag-reviewer` fire. If the gardener schedule is still enabled, the gardener should then offer to self-disable (its loop_end will also fire once the molecule children all close).
- **Any box fails** → do NOT clear the gate. Comment what is missing and ensure the responsible critic has bounced to its target step. Sign-off waits for the redo.

> A critic that merely *ran* is not a pass — only a recorded score >= 8 counts. If a critic verdict is missing, treat that critic as failing and block sign-off.
